course: NISM Series XXIV: AML and CFT Provisions in Securities Markets
unit_name: Introduction to Anti Money Laundering (AML), Combating the Financing of Terrorism (CFT) and Proliferation Financing (PF)
overview: This chapter is the foundation of the entire NISM Series XXIV exam. It introduces you to the 'World of Financial Crimes.' You will learn how criminals hide their illegal money (Money Laundering), how terrorists get funded (CFT), and how weapons of mass destruction are financed (PF). For the NISM exam, it is crucial to understand these basics because all the laws (PMLA) and SEBI guidelines discussed in later chapters are built to solve the problems mentioned here.

complete_concept_explanation.basic_meaning: Money Laundering is the process of making 'Dirty Money' (money earned from crime) look like 'Clean Money' (money earned from a legal business).
complete_concept_explanation.detailed_explanation: When criminals earn money from illegal activities like drug trafficking, kidnapping, or fraud, they cannot use it openly in the bank because the government will ask, 'Where did this come from?'. To avoid this, they 'wash' the money through the financial system so it looks legitimate. This is called Money Laundering. Anti-Money Laundering (AML) refers to the laws and rules made by the government to stop this activity.
complete_concept_explanation.why_this_is_important: In the exam, you will often get questions on the definition of ML. Practically, if you work in a stockbroking firm, you must know what ML is so you can identify if a client is trying to hide illegal wealth.
complete_concept_explanation.real_life_indian_example: Suppose an illegal lottery operator in a village earns ₹50 Lakhs in cash. He cannot buy a luxury apartment in Mumbai directly with this cash. He gives this cash to 100 different friends (Smurfing) to deposit small amounts into their bank accounts. Then, he gathers it all to show it as 'business income' from a fake consultancy firm. This is Money Laundering.
exam_traps: ML is not just about avoiding tax; it is primarily about hiding the criminal origin of the money.
Remember that the activity must be connected to a 'Predicate Offence' (a crime that generated the money).
The term 'Laundering' comes from the actual use of launderettes (washing machines) by criminals in the past to hide cash.
complete_concept_explanation.memory_trick: Think of ML as a 'Laundry Service'—Dirty clothes (Criminal money) go in, and Clean clothes (Legitimate money) come out.

complete_concept_explanation.basic_meaning: Criminals use a 3-step process to launder money: Placement, Layering, and Integration.
complete_concept_explanation.detailed_explanation: Step 1: Placement – The 'Dirty' cash is first introduced into the legal financial system. This is the riskiest stage for criminals. Step 2: Layering – The money is moved through complex transactions (like buying shares, selling them, and moving money between accounts) to hide the original trail. Step 3: Integration – The money now appears clean and is 'integrated' into the economy, often used to buy luxury assets like real estate.
complete_concept_explanation.why_this_is_important: NISM loves asking questions like 'Which stage is the most complex?' or 'In which stage is the money moved between many bank accounts?'.
complete_concept_explanation.formula_explanation: While not a mathematical formula, it shows that all three steps must happen for the money to be fully 'clean.'
complete_concept_explanation.step_by_step_calculation_example: Numerical Example of 'Structuring' (Placement Stage): The Indian government requires banks to report cash deposits above ₹10 Lakhs. A criminal has ₹45 Lakhs cash. Instead of one deposit, he makes 5 deposits of ₹9 Lakhs each in different branches on different days. This 'break-up' to stay below the limit is called Structuring.
complete_concept_explanation.real_life_indian_example: If a criminal buys stocks in a fake company (Placement), then keeps buying and selling different shares across 10 different broker accounts (Layering), and finally uses the profit to buy a bungalow in Alibaug (Integration).
exam_traps: Placement is the 'Riskiest' stage because large cash is involved.
Layering is the 'Most Complex' stage because it involves many layers of transactions.
Integration is where the money becomes 'Clean' and re-enters the normal economy.
complete_concept_explanation.memory_trick: Remember the acronym 'P-L-I': Put it in (Placement), Layer it up (Layering), and In you go (Integration).

complete_concept_explanation.concept: 3. Combating the Financing of Terrorism (CFT) & Proliferation Financing (PF)
complete_concept_explanation.basic_meaning: CFT is about stopping money from going to terrorists. PF is about stopping money from going to build weapons like nuclear bombs.
complete_concept_explanation.detailed_explanation: Terrorist Financing (TF) is different from Money Laundering. In ML, the 'Source' of money is always illegal. In TF, the source can be legal (like donations or salary) but the 'End Use' is illegal (to kill people). Proliferation Financing (PF) specifically deals with money used for Weapons of Mass Destruction (WMD) like chemical, biological, or nuclear weapons.
complete_concept_explanation.why_this_is_important: Important because intermediaries (brokers) must screen clients against global 'Sanctions Lists' to ensure they aren't terrorists.
complete_concept_explanation.real_life_indian_example: If a legitimate businessman in India sends ₹1 Lakh to a banned organization in another country for 'charity,' but that money is used to buy explosives, this is a case of Terrorist Financing. Even if the money was earned legally, the sender is liable.
exam_traps: In ML, the money is always 'Dirty' at the start. In TF, the money can be 'Clean' at the start.
PF is only about 'Weapons of Mass Destruction.' If the question says 'buying guns for a robbery,' it is not PF, it is general crime.
complete_concept_explanation.memory_trick: ML = Hide the Past (where money came from). CFT = Block the Future (where money is going).

complete_concept_explanation.basic_meaning: Countries around the world joined hands to create rules against ML and TF. The most important one is FATF.
complete_concept_explanation.detailed_explanation: 1. FATF (Financial Action Task Force): Established in 1989 by G7 countries. It is the global watchdog. It issued '40 Recommendations' which are the standard for all countries. 2. Vienna Convention (1988): Focused on stopping money from Drug Trafficking. 3. Basel Committee: Focuses on banks having strong internal controls. 4. Egmont Group: A group of 'Financial Intelligence Units' (like our FIU-IND) that share data globally.
complete_concept_explanation.why_this_is_important: Direct questions are asked on the year of FATF establishment (1989) and the focus of the Vienna Convention (Drugs).
complete_concept_explanation.real_life_indian_example: India is a member of FATF. If India does not follow FATF rules, it might be put on the 'Grey List,' which makes it difficult for Indian banks to do business with other countries.
exam_traps: The Vienna Convention (1988) was the FIRST international treaty to address money laundering.
FATF does not make laws; it makes 'Recommendations.' Each country then makes its own law based on these (like India made PMLA).

important_differences.clear_explanation: 1. Source of Funds: In ML, the money is always from a crime. In TF, money can come from legal donations or illegal activities. 2. Motivation: ML is motivated by PROFIT. TF is motivated by IDEOLOGY/POLITICAL reasons. 3. Trail: ML aims to hide the origin of money. TF aims to hide the destination of money.
Placement is putting cash into the bank for the first time. Layering is moving that money around between many accounts/products to confuse the police.

frequently_asked_exam_areas: Definition and order of ML stages: Placement -> Layering -> Integration.
Difference between ML and TF funds source.
Focus area of the Vienna Convention 1988 (Drug trafficking).
quick_revision_summary: Money Laundering makes dirty money look clean.
Stages are Placement (Riskiest), Layering (Most Complex), and Integration (Final).
CFT deals with the 'End Use' of money for terror.
FATF is the global standard-setter established in 1989.
India follows these global standards via PMLA and SEBI guidelines.
